A quick reference for the models introduced in the [R Tutorial](r_tutorial.qmd).

## Non-linear responses: GAM

A Generalized Additive Model (GAM) replaces the linear covariate effect with a smooth function, allowing a non-linear response.

$$
y_t = \mathrm{Pois}(
  \underbrace{\color{#d53f8c}{\lambda_t}}_{\textstyle\color{#d53f8c}{\text{rate parameter}}}
)
$$

$$
\underbrace{\color{#d69e2e}{\log(\lambda_t)}}_{\textstyle\color{#d69e2e}{\text{log link}}} = \underbrace{\color{#2b6cb0}{c}}_{\textstyle\color{#2b6cb0}{\text{constant}}}
  \;+\; \underbrace{\color{#2f855a}{f(x_{1,t})}}_{\textstyle\color{#2f855a}{\text{smooth covariate effect}}}
  \;+\; \underbrace{\color{#c05621}{\beta_2 y_{t-1}}}_{\textstyle\color{#c05621}{\text{AR: lag-1}}}
$$

- $y_t$ — the observed count at time $t$
- $\lambda_t$ — the Poisson rate parameter
- $f(x_{1,t})$ — a smooth function of the covariate, estimated from the data rather than constrained to a straight line; `s(mintemp)` in the model formula
- $c$, $\beta_2 y_{t-1}$ — the same constant and AR terms as before

**Note:** $f$ is estimated on the log scale, so view the response on the scale of abundance with `plot_predictions()`.
